newsitem.title: UKRAINE: IMF pleased with Ukraine on budget, tax reforms.
newsitem.headline: IMF pleased with Ukraine on budget, tax reforms.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund said on Friday it had made progress during this week's mission to Ukraine to discuss the much delayed budget.
Successful passage of the budget and a package of tax reforms to underpin it would pave the way for a $2.5 to $3 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) from the IMF.

"Both the (Ukrainian) authorities and the mission were pleased by the progress made in the week of discussions, including progress made on the EFF," the IMF's senior resident representative Patrick Lenain told Reuters.
He said the mission met Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko and Deputy Prime Minister Serhiy Tyhypko, who is in charge of economic policy, and other members of government.
Further IMF talks would be held when President Leonid Kuchma travels to Washington for meetings in mid-May, Lenain added.
The Ukrainian authorities have said the budget would be reviewed in mid-May and implemented by the end of May.
